name: HORSE
description: HORSE is a mixed poker game format that rotates through five different poker variants in a fixed sequence. The acronym stands for Hold'em, Omaha Hi/Lo, Razz, Seven Card Stud, and Eight-or-Better (Stud Hi/Lo). Popular in major tournaments like the World Series of Poker, HORSE tests a player's versatility across multiple poker disciplines. All games are played in Fixed-Limit format.
duration: Variable (rotates games every round or time period)

history.origins: Developed in the United States as a way to test poker players' skills across multiple variants. Became prominent in high-stakes cash games and tournament play.
timeline: 1970s-1980s: Mixed poker games gain popularity in high-stakes cash games.
2002: HORSE event added to the World Series of Poker.
2006: $50,000 HORSE Championship becomes a prestigious WSOP event.
Present: HORSE remains a staple in major poker tournaments and online poker rooms.
history.cultural: Represents the pinnacle of poker skill testing, as players must master five distinct games rather than specializing in one.
history.evolution: HORSE evolved from the tradition of dealer's choice poker, where players would rotate through different variants. The fixed rotation ensures all players must be proficient in multiple poker styles.

setup.dealing: Deal according to current game in rotation (Hold'em, Omaha, etc.).
setup.equipment: Standard deck, poker chips, dealer button.

rules.objective: Win chips/money by winning pots in each of the five poker variants.
rules.gameplay: HORSE = rotation of Hold'em, Omaha, Razz, Stud, Stud Eight-or-better. Each variant 1 orbit; switch after each. Same betting structure. Lowest chip count at end loses.
keyRules: All five games are played as fixed-limit. Hold'em and Omaha use blinds; Razz, Stud, and Stud 8 use antes and a compulsory bring-in.
Rotation is fixed: H then O then R then S then E. A complete round of each game is played (every player has one deal or button) before switching.
Hand rankings and showdown rules follow the current variant: standard high for Hold'em and Stud; Omaha 8 and Stud 8 split high and low (eight or better for low).
With more than seven players, the last in order sit out for stud games so the deck does not run out.

strategy.basic: Learn the fundamentals of each individual game before attempting HORSE. Focus on starting hand selection for each variant.
strategy.intermediate: Adjust your strategy as the game rotates. For example, tight-aggressive play works in Hold'em, but Razz requires different hand values.
strategy.advanced: Exploit opponents' weaknesses in specific games. If an opponent is weak in Razz, apply pressure when that game is in rotation.
tips: Razz and Stud Hi/Lo are often the weakest games for Hold'em specialists. Study these carefully.
In Omaha Hi/Lo, always aim to 'scoop' (win both high and low) rather than just half the pot.
